newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's Aleman to press US on immigrant rights.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's Aleman to press US on immigrant rights.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman said on Friday he would appeal to the United States for improved immigration status for Nicaraguan immigrants when he attends a United Nations environment summit there next week.
Aleman will spend Tuesday and Wednesday in Washington, where he plans to intercede on behalf of some 70,000 immigrants who risk deportation under new U.S. immigration laws.

Before leaving for next week's special environment summit in New York, Aleman told reporters he would ask for temporary status for those immigrants most in danger of being deported and permanent status for some 40,000 to 45,000 who moved to the United States during the last decade.
Official sources estimate that 25,000 to 30,000 Nicaraguans who moved to the United States since 1980 may be obliged to return home in the near term.
During his visit Aleman will meet U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno and officials from the U.S. State Department, including Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs, Thomas Pickering.
